caption_hook: 🌿 A no-strings cash trial in the Peruvian Amazon cut food insecurity from 73% to 26% + 3 more wins you missed 👇
question: Pick a number: which story made you smile most, 1, 2, 3 or 4?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves big ideas
first_comment: Bonus: many people in the Amazon trial spent part of the money on education and solar power. What would you spend an extra £2 a day on? 🌿

stories.headline: A no-strings cash trial cut food insecurity from 73% to 26%
stories.summary: For 2 years, 211 people in 3 Indigenous Amazon communities got about £2 a day to spend freely. Food insecurity dropped sharply and 90% took up greener farming practices.
stories.why: It was small, with no control group, but the charity behind it plans to expand.

stories.headline: Seabird poo helps reefs grow up to 2.5 times faster
stories.summary: On 28 tropical islands, reefs beside thriving seabird colonies grew up to 2.5x faster than those near rat-infested atolls, and made more sand to build the islands.
stories.why: Bringing back seabirds and native plants could help some atolls keep pace with rising seas.

stories.headline: A plant-covered Bangladeshi rug factory won a top world prize
stories.summary: Draped in plants and gardens, Rangpur's Green Field factory cools itself naturally and gives workers views, a medical centre, daycare and a canteen. It won the RIBA International Prize.
stories.why: Its architect says a factory should restore people's energy, not drain it.

stories.stat_label: miles flown to his new family
stories.headline: An orphaned baby walrus found alone on a beach was saved
stories.summary: Annautaq, a 5-month-old calf, was hiding beside the remains of 2 adult walruses on a remote Alaska beach. Rescuers cared for him, then flew him 4,000 miles to join 3 walruses in Florida.
stories.why: Calves need their mothers for a year, so he'll grow up with an experienced walrus 'aunt'.

fun_fact: The walrus calf's name, Annautaq, means 'axe' in Iñupiaq, honouring his rescuer's father.
